In [[mathematics]], the ''i''th '''Bass number''' of a [[module (mathematics)|module]] ''M'' over a [[local ring]] ''R'' with [[residue field]] ''k'' is the ''k''-dimension of <math>\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(k,M)</math>. More generally the Bass number <math>\mu_i(p,M)</math> of a module ''M'' over a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'' at a [[prime ideal]] ''p'' is the Bass number of the [[localization of a module|localization]] of ''M'' for the [[Localization (commutative algebra)#Localization of a ring|localization]] of ''R'' (with respect to the prime ''p''). Bass numbers were introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink= Hyman Bass|last=Bass|first=Hyman|year=1963|loc=p.11}}.

The Bass numbers describe the minimal [[injective resolution]] of a [[finitely-generated module]] ''M'' over a [[Noetherian ring]]: for each prime ideal ''p'' there is a corresponding [[indecomposable module|indecomposable]] [[injective module]], and the number of times this occurs in the ''i''th term of a minimal resolution of ''M'' is the Bass number <math>\mu_i(p,M)</math>.
